records.h: Pill ▸ Open → pick a resident, an ARC-only .ifc FROM IFC (parses via the same engine the Viewer uses, always filtered to ARC — never a second parser, never a non-ARC discipline), or a local .db/.ifc. Either way it walks the structure (STR) and seeds the ARC bom-graph — no separate drop panel.

Pill ▸ Open ▸ Open 2D drawings (.dxf)… , select every sheet of the set. For a low-cost single-storey house drawn in CAD: Open 2D drawings from PDF drawing (.pdf)… and pick the one PDF (a scan has no lines to read and is refused). The 2D pill (key D ) then shows or hides the panel; its X closes it the same way and nothing is lost. Shift+D is Drawing metadata. A raw set plays its arrangement ( Arrange replays it). Colours: yellow = defaulted, not yours yet · orange = inferred · red outline = required · solid = yours. Accept all (when orange rows are listed too: Accept stated + read , then check the orange rows and Accept inferred ), then state what is red: the set name (once), a second height per elevation, what each layer is (split by sheet where it differs), body heights, Exclude a box. A sheet card's Sheet button shows the whole sheet as drawn, its metadata drawn on it and the open yellow rows as rings; Save SVG / Print . The chip reads Qualifies (or each blocking item is listed); tick Complete the building if wanted, then Convert . Pill ▸ Export ▸ Viewer database (.db) , open it in the Viewer for 3D / 4D / 5D. It never invents: what no sheet states is asked for or left out and listed. Full guide with screenshots ↗

records.n: Outliner — ARC leads, ONE Disc tab
records.h: The one panel is the surface: Building ▸ Storey ▸ Room ▸ discipline ▸ class ▸ element (real door/AABB-qualified rooms; door-less storeys read "· layer"). Disciplines PRESENT in the building drill into their real elements; disciplines ABSENT from it (e.g. no MEP was ever extracted) show up in the SAME tree with a "▶ walk" click — one Disc facet, not a separate tab. The find box filters across every category, auto-expands past any collapsed branch to reveal a match, and highlights the exact matching row.

go.hkey: guide:Outliner — ARC leads, ONE Disc tab

records.h: Click a discipline node — present or absent — to walk it: STR surfaces the structural walk; an MEP-family disc routes when anchored, else it refuses honestly ("no walk") — never a fabricated run. "▶▶ Walk ALL Disciplines" walks every absent one at once (x-ray reveal).

The grid is the primary handle. Grid shows/hides the datums; Move Grid drags a gridline so attached walls RECOMPOSE — stretch, not scale (openings stay host-constrained). While dragging, every governed wall LIVE-TINTS: blue = moves rigidly, orange = stretches. Ctrl/Cmd+click any tinted element (before or during a drag) to opt it OUT for this drag — it turns green and sits still, bidirectional (click again to re-include). Opt-outs reset every time you re-enter Move Grid.

Every move/stretch is checked and reported (never auto-reverted). RED = a hard stop: a new clash, a door sliding off its wall, or a wall stretched narrower than a hosted door's own width (door-crush). ORANGE = a suggestion: a neighbour now sitting too close (clearance), or a real touching neighbour left behind by the edit (abuts-realign) — shown for now, accept/ignore wiring is next.

Sketch a profile, Insert a catalog component (assemble, don't draw), Cut an opening, Route an MEP run, Fillet an edge. Every edit is one signed op in the log. Sketching a 4-point rect/square shows live W/H/∠ fields once the shape closes — type a new width, height, or corner angle and Enter re-solves the WHOLE profile from that one number (a rectangle at 90°, a parallelogram at any other angle). Cycle to Circle mode for a click-center-then-radius circle (typed radius too) — Extrude sweeps it into a real cylinder, not a tessellated polygon stand-in. A click that lands near an earlier point in the SAME sketch welds the new point exactly onto it instead of adding a near-duplicate a few cm off.

Select an object (M) to arm the move gizmo — drag an axis handle to translate it, snapping to the grid; arrow keys nudge by a typed step, or type an exact delta mid-drag. Drag an empty-space marquee (or shift-click) to select several objects and move them together as a group. While dragging, the handle also snaps to nearby vertices/edges/face-centers of OTHER objects (not just the grid), with a marker showing what it snapped to. T arms the rotate ring (drag it — Shift for free rotation, otherwise 15° snap); S arms scale — drag an edge-anchored cube handle to stretch a single catalog component non-uniformly. Every move/rotate/scale is one signed op, undo restores the prior placement exactly.
Scrub the bottom timeline to fold the model to any point; Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+⇧Z undo/redo. Geometry is a deterministic fold over the signed op-log.

Your edits auto-save to the signed op-log (restored on your next visit, per building). Pill ▸ Export offers Native .db (the full-fidelity signed op-log, conventionally saved into IFC/BimDB/ — re-opens via Open ▸ local .db), Viewer database (.db — opens in the Viewer), IFC4, a BCF 2.1 issue, or 2D drawings (DXF).

Pill ▸ Teams (top-right of the bar) — click to see who else is editing THIS MODEL right now: presence dots + a blame/chat pane over the design op-log. Off by default; first click turns it on, same as ?teams=1. This is authoring collaboration (Modeller + ERP chrome) — a different feature from "HBA" (tenancy/IoT/occupancy pills), which is a separate Viewer-only operations overlay for a live building and does not exist in the Modeller. v1 scope: presence works across tabs/windows of the same browser profile only (it rides a same-profile broadcast channel) — a genuinely different person on a different device will not see your presence yet; that needs a server relay, not yet built.
